uncertainty.method: May-year block bootstrap; fixed fitted model and threshold

source_audit.source_decision: Keep ERA5 for assessed modelling and unchanged May targets. NASA POWER is a source sensitivity audit only, not a way to increase event prevalence.
source_audit.nasa_time_standard: UTC daily boundaries differ from ERA5 Asia/Kolkata. Provider comparison is descriptive and not a matched station validation.

provider_benchmark.target: IMD-inspired proxy using NASA temperatures and its own frozen 1981–2010 reference
provider_benchmark.selection_note: Architecture and weight-mode fixed from the ERA5 v2 selection before NASA evaluation; only training, early stopping and calibration are source-specific.
limitations: These scores are not comparable as an improvement over ERA5 because the target data product and daily boundaries differ.

52 lag features use six meteorological variables, seven lagged departures, previous proxy and calendar; early solar responses are unavailable and are excluded for every year. NASA wind is 2m, ERA5 is 10m.
The benchmark is not validated against official station declarations or live warnings.
